sections.sectionText: ****If interested, contact Chloe Morrell chloem@illinois.edu for an interview.*** Title: Performance Nutrition Experience with Illini Athletics and Illini Fuel. This 2-credit hour course provides students with an immersive, hands-on opportunity to work alongside Illini Athletics and the Illini Fuel program at the University of Illinois. Students will gain valuable experience in performance nutrition, contributing to the preparation, delivery, and management of athlete-focused nutritional support. Enrollment requires successfully passing an interview process followed by a background check conducted by the Department of Intercollegiate Athletics prior to the first week of class. Students will commit to ~6 hours per week (totaling 100 hours) over the semester, including early morning and late evening shifts. Attendance and participation are critical, with each 2-hour shift contributing 2% toward the final grade. Students must arrive on time with a positive "can-do" attitude and remain until formal dismissal to earn this credit. This course is ideal for students passionate about performance nutrition, seeking to develop practical skills and gain professional experience in a dynamic environment that directly supports athletic performance and recovery.

sections.sectionText: FOOD SAFETY AUDITING, INSPECTIONS AND ASSESSMENTS: This course introduces students to food safety auditing, inspections, and assessments (AIA) across regulatory, third‑party, and industry contexts. Students explore how food safety systems are governed at local, national, and international levels and practice foundational auditing skills through applied, scenario‑based learning. Emphasis is placed on risk‑based thinking, professional judgment, and effective communication of audit findings. The course will be offered as part of a multi‑institution cohort, enabling shared guest speakers, collaborative activities, and exposure to diverse food systems.

AI-ENABLED SUSTAINABLE FOOD PROCESSING: The future of food manufacturing is digital, intelligent, and sustainable. As the global food system faces growing challenges related to climate change, resource constraints, supply chain disruptions, and increasing consumer demand for transparency and quality, the integration of artificial intelligence and sustainability-driven innovation is transforming how food is produced and processed. In this course, students will learn how AI, digital technologies, and sustainability principles are reshaping modern food processing systems. Students will explore how AI can optimize processing operations, reduce energy and water use, minimize waste, enhance food safety, improve product consistency, and strengthen resilient supply chains. Through case studies and applied data exercises, students will gain experience with digital sensing, predictive modeling, resource-efficient manufacturing strategies, circular processing approaches, and data-driven quality control. By integrating concepts from food engineering, food chemistry, sustainability assessment, and data analytics, students will develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to design and evaluate next-generation, climate-smart food manufacturing systems. Pre-requisites: Introductory Food Processing or Food Engineering, Introductory Statistics.
